title: September starter · A skill worth learning
description: Original supplementary English practice for the new term. Write independently first, then improve two sentences. A fictional example is welcome. No deadline has been set yet.
objectives: Explain a choice with reasons and an example.
Connect ideas clearly and revise your own writing.
source: Original practice by Rory’s English; not a way2go! 8 textbook exercise.

tasks.prompt: 1 · Plan (2 minutes). Choose a skill someone your age could learn this year: a language, cooking, coding, a sport or another idea. Write three short notes: the skill; why it is useful; one possible difficulty. You may invent the person.

2 · Write (10–12 minutes). Write 100–130 words for a school blog: “A skill worth learning”. Explain your choice, give one specific example of its value, and suggest a realistic first step. Use because and although to connect ideas. Optional start: “One skill worth learning is … because …”. Keep this first draft so Rory can see your starting point.

3 · Improve (5 minutes). Copy two sentences from your draft, then write a clearer or more accurate version of each. Explain one change briefly. Check verb forms, articles and prepositions. Finish with: “I worked independently” or name any help you used (dictionary, AI hint or another person). Then press Send answers to Rory.

title: This week · Healthy habits voice practice
description: First, have an 8–10-minute conversation about healthy habits with your AI partner. Then prepare and record your short individual talk in this app. Listen back, choose your improved take, and send it to Rory with the button below. The conversation is saved separately. Keep examples general, with no private health details. No deadline has been set yet.
objectives: Speak clearly for about two minutes without reading a complete script.
Explain healthy choices with reasons, examples and a realistic challenge.
source: Original Rory’s English practice linked to the published way2go! 8 Unit 1 theme “Healthy and happy”; not a textbook exercise or publisher recording.

tasks.prompt: 1 · Plan (5 minutes). Make short notes for a talk called “Two habits for a healthier school week”. Choose two habits linked to sleep, food, movement, study breaks, stress or another suitable idea. For each habit, note: what it is; how it may help body or mind; one realistic example. Add one challenge and a possible solution. Write keywords only, not a full script.

2 · Speak and record (8–10 minutes). Record a 1½–2 minute individual talk using your notes. Include an introduction, both habits, one challenge with a solution, and a short conclusion. Use at least three linking phrases such as “firstly”, “for example”, “however”, “as a result” or “overall”. Try once, listen back, then record one improved version. Use the recorder above to send your chosen take to Rory. In this box, tell Rory which linking phrases you used.
3 · Reflect (3 minutes). Write one thing that sounded good and one specific target for your next talk, for example pace, pronunciation, grammar or clearer examples. Name any help you used.

title: Next week · A wellbeing idea for school
description: Start from 30 September. Discuss a school wellbeing idea with your AI partner for 8–10 minutes, then write your own short semi-formal email. The conversation is saved separately for Rory; submit your email here. Keep your example general, without private medical information. No deadline has been set yet.
objectives: Organise a semi-formal email with a clear purpose, proposal and conclusion.
Support an idea with reasons while using an appropriate register.
source: Original Rory’s English practice linked to the published way2go! 8 Unit 1 theme “Healthy and happy”; not a textbook exercise.

tasks.prompt: 1 · Plan (4 minutes). Imagine your school wants one new activity to support students’ wellbeing. Choose one realistic idea, for example a quiet break room, a walking club, a phone-free lunch or a short stress-management workshop. Note: the current problem; your proposal; two benefits; one possible concern and your answer to it.

2 · Write (12 minutes). Write a 130–160-word email to a teacher or school representative. Include a subject line, greeting and closing. Explain why you are writing, describe your proposal, give two reasons or examples, address one possible concern, and finish with a clear request or next step. Use at least three linking phrases and keep the tone polite and semi-formal.

3 · Check and improve (4 minutes). Copy one sentence you changed and give the improved version. Then confirm: 130–160 words; clear paragraphs; suitable greeting and closing; verb forms, articles and prepositions checked. Finish with “I worked independently” or name any help you used, then send your answers to Rory.
